problems.title: A signed double-angle tangent
problems.question: $\cos(\alpha-\pi/2)=-2/3$ and $3\pi/2<\alpha<2\pi$. Find tan 2α.
problems.idea: Use the trigonometric identity or a coordinate model, with the domain checked.

problems.title: Complementary-angle simplification
problems.question: Simplify $\cos^2(\pi/3+\alpha)/\tan^2(\pi/6-\alpha)+\sin^2(\pi/3+\alpha)\tan^2(\pi/6-\alpha)$.
problems.idea: Use the trigonometric identity or a coordinate model, with the domain checked.
formulas: Put t=π/3+α. Then $\pi/6-\alpha=\pi/2-t$, and its tangent is cot t.
steps: On the original domain both sin t and cos t are nonzero. The first term becomes cos²t/cot²t=sin²t; the second becomes sin²t cot²t=cos²t. Their sum is 1.

problems.title: Distance to a side from above a triangle
problems.question: ABC has AB=13, BC=14, AC=15. D is midpoint of AC, and DM is perpendicular to the triangle plane. M is √52 from BC. Find DM.
problems.idea: Use the trigonometric identity or a coordinate model, with the domain checked.
formulas: Heron gives $S=\sqrt{21\cdot8\cdot7\cdot6}=84$. The altitude from A to BC is $2S/BC=12$.
steps: Since D is midpoint of AC and C lies on BC, D’s distance to BC is 6. The perpendicular-plane distance relation is dist(M, BC)²=DM²+dist(D, BC)². Thus 52=DM²+36.

problems.title: Angle between two cube lines
problems.question: K is midpoint of DD₁ in cube ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁. Find the cosine of the acute angle between CK and A₁D.
problems.idea: Use the trigonometric identity or a coordinate model, with the domain checked.
steps: Direction vectors are u=(−1,0,1/2), v=(0,1,−1). Their dot product is −1/2. The acute line angle uses |u·v|/(|u||v|)=(1/2)/(√5/2·√2).

problems.title: Point-to-plane distance inside a cube
problems.question: A unit cube has T, P, Q the centres of faces AA₁B₁B, A₁B₁C₁D₁, BB₁C₁C. Find the distance from P to plane ATQ.
problems.idea: Use the trigonometric identity or a coordinate model, with the domain checked.
steps: The plane equation is −x+y+z=0. The distance of P is|−1/2+1/2+1|/√3=1/√3.

problems.title: Minimum of a positive reciprocal
problems.question: Find the minimum of $3/(-2\cos^2x+6\sin x+9)$.
problems.idea: Use the trigonometric identity or a coordinate model, with the domain checked.
formulas: Put s=sin x∈[−1,1]. The denominator is $2s^2+6s+7$.
steps: It is strictly increasing on this interval because its derivative 4s+6 is positive. Its minimum and maximum are 3 and 15, so it is always positive. The reciprocal is smallest at denominator 15, attained when sin x=1.

problems.title: Trigonometric reciprocals with degree angles
problems.question: Evaluate $1/\cos290°+(1/\sin165°+1/\cos165°)^2+1/(\sqrt3\sin250°)$.
problems.idea: Use the trigonometric identity or a coordinate model, with the domain checked.
steps: The other two terms sum to(√3cos20°−sin 20°)/(√3sin20°cos 20°). The numerator is 2cos50°=2sin40°; the denominator is(√3/2)sin 40°. Their quotient is 4/√3.
